items.action_detail: Exploitation is plausible and impact is high

items.title: PoC released: CVE-2026-10053
items.description: Reproducible lab for CVE-2026-10053 (GitLab npm package-registry path traversal -> arbitrary file write as git). Vulnerable 19.2.1 vs patched 19.2.2, deterministic oracle.
items.action_detail: Exploitation is plausible and impact is high
items.ai_summary: A path traversal vulnerability exists in the npm package-registry component of GitLab versions up to 19.2.1, allowing arbitrary file write operations under the git user context. A public proof-of-concept exploits this flaw using a deterministic oracle to manipulate file paths during package uploads. Successful exploitation can lead to remote code execution or system compromise. Administrators must upgrade immediately to version 19.2.2 or later.
items.why_it_matters: GitLab administrators must apply version 19.2.2 immediately to prevent full system compromise via arbitrary file writes.

items.title: PoC released: CVE-2026-15718
items.description: PoC exploit chain for CVE-2026-15718: SpiderMonkey wasm baseline compiler array.fill missing-sync -> invalid pointer -> addrOf/fakeobj -> arbitrary R/W -> RCE
items.cwe_name: CWE-763 Release of Invalid Pointer or Reference
items.priority_rationale: Public PoC on GitHub · EPSS 0.4% · CVSS 4.3
items.action_detail: Exploitation is plausible and impact is high
items.ai_summary: A missing synchronization issue in the SpiderMonkey wasm baseline compiler array.fill function leads to an invalid pointer vulnerability, designated as CVE-2026-15718. An attacker can leverage this primitive to construct addrOf and fakeobj capabilities, resulting in arbitrary read and write access and ultimately remote code execution. A proof-of-concept exploit chain has been released publicly. Users must apply vendor patches as soon as they become available.
items.why_it_matters: Browser vendors and users should update vulnerable SpiderMonkey runtimes promptly to block arbitrary code execution chains.
